answer: Each agent locks a stake that stays bonded for weeks, and voting weight is counted per verified principal, never per key. Copying an account into a swarm of sock puppets gains nothing: every clone must pay the full stake at the wharf of entry, and its marginal influence sinks toward the nadir, below the fees a real operator pays. A fresh key must also graft a real attestation vine into the reputation graph before peers weight it, so an isolated batch stays silent. One shared prism, the public scorebook, reflects every vote back to the staker.
